A positive ln ⁡ B 10 \ln B_{10} value for a model means it is preferred over Λ \Lambda CDM. All relative ln ⁡ B \ln B uncertainties include a systematic contribution of 0.13 from the Λ \Lambda CDM analysis. We use the DES-Dovekie + DESI DR2 BAO + CC + CMB + BBN constraint in all cases (Section 3.3 ). We also consider the SH0ES anchor ( Breuval et al., 2024 ) or the three H 0 H_{0} anchors that are independent of the SNIa absolute magnitude, imposed jointly and labelled “Excl. SNIa”. We use three different cases for the DES-Dovekie sample: DES alone, DES + legacy, and DES + legacy with a magnitude offset of Δ ​ M legacy \Delta M_{\mathrm{legacy}} on the legacy SNIa. The w 0 / A w_{0}/A column shows w 0 w_{0} for CPL and A A for the exp model, while the w a / z 1 w_{a}/z_{1} column shows w a w_{a} for CPL and z 1 z_{1} for the exp model. Missing model parameters are marked with a dash, while “Unc.” indicates parameters that are largely unconstrained by the data, with a posterior spanning essentially the whole prior range (Table 1 ). Uncertainties follow the convention of Table 2 , and one-sided limits enclose 68% of the posterior. The triangle plots corresponding to these results are shown in Appendix C . The Bayesian evidence of each considered model ( exp and CPL) is shown in Table 3 relative to the Λ \Lambda CDM control, whose uncertainty contributes a systematic component of 0.13 to all the stated ln ⁡ B 10 \ln B_{10} uncertainties. Without relying on any local H 0 H_{0} anchor, | ln ⁡ B 10 | ≤ 1.22 \lvert\ln B_{10}\rvert\leq 1.22 for the exp model, implying at most weak evidence for or against it – though it is generally disfavoured in this case. The results for the CPL model are critically dependent on whether we include the legacy SNIa. Without them, CPL is disfavoured by 1.79 natural units (nats). Including them at face value leads to a 1.70 nat preference for CPL, but including them and allowing an arbitrary recalibration reverts this to a 1.39 nat preference against CPL. These results clarify that without local H 0 H_{0} anchors, the Bayesian evidence for CPL largely comes from adding the legacy SNIa at face value, which we have argued elsewhere is most likely not appropriate ( Ormondroyd et al., 2026 , cf.) . The predicted H 0 H_{0} in the CPL model (without H 0 H_{0} anchors) is always similar to H 0 SPA H_{0}^{\mathrm{SPA}} , but this is true in the exp model only if we include the legacy SNIa at face value. If we neglect them altogether or add them with arbitrary recalibration, the predicted H 0 H_{0} is almost 69 ​ km ​ s − 1 ​ Mpc − 1 69\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}} , which given the uncertainties is marginally compatible with H 0 SH0ES H_{0}^{\mathrm{SH0ES}} (e.g. DES alone gives H 0 = 68.83 ± 2.02 ​ km ​ s − 1 ​ Mpc − 1 H_{0}=68.83\pm 2.02\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}} , which is within 2 ​ σ 2\sigma of SH0ES). It is therefore possible to combine local H 0 H_{0} anchors with the other data only for the exp model and even then only if the legacy SNIa are excluded or recalibrated. We cannot add local H 0 H_{0} anchors if we use the CPL model, regardless of how we treat the legacy SNIa. If we take these at face value, we cannot add local H 0 H_{0} anchors for either model – or indeed for any model with standard r d r_{\rm d} . The CPL model was not proposed as a solution to the Hubble tension, but rather as a way to better fit available BAO and uncalibrated SNIa data consistently with the CMB. We find that when constraining the CPL model with DES + legacy, ( w 0 , w a ) (w_{0},w_{a}) is in 3.36 ​ σ 3.36\sigma tension with the Λ \Lambda CDM limit, which we obtain from the improvement in the fit when w 0 w_{0} and w a w_{a} are freed ( Δ ​ χ 2 = 14.32 \Delta\chi^{2}=14.32 ), converted to a Gaussian significance for two additional parameters. However, this w 0 w_{0} – w a w_{a} tension gets reduced to 2.13 ​ σ 2.13\sigma upon removing the legacy SNIa, while allowing an arbitrary recalibration of them relative to DES leads to 2.21 ​ σ 2.21\sigma tension. Both cases are plausibly consistent with Λ \Lambda CDM. The departure from Λ \Lambda CDM expectations claimed by DESI Collaboration (2025) is therefore reliant on the legacy SNIa ( Ormondroyd et al., 2026 ) . Indeed, the actual BAO observables (angular scale and redshift depth) can be fit jointly with the CMB at an acceptable total χ 2 \chi^{2} if SNIa are neglected ( Banik et al., 2026c ) . On the other hand, their work found that Λ \Lambda CDM faces a 3.07 ​ σ 3.07\sigma CMB–BAO tension in the ( H 0 ​ r d , Ω m ) (H_{0}r_{\rm d},\Omega_{\rm m}) parameter space without considering SNIa. Combined with our result in Figure 2 , this is suggestive of a growing anomaly between CMB-calibrated Λ \Lambda CDM predictions and observations as we move towards lower redshift. When adding the SNIa-independent H 0 H_{0} anchors, the exp model is disfavoured compared to Λ \Lambda CDM if we add the legacy SNIa at face value, but this dataset combination is not valid because the legacy SNIa cannot be reconciled with local H 0 H_{0} measurements in any plausible model with standard r d r_{\rm d} . In the other cases, the non-SH0ES anchors on H 0 H_{0} lead to a preference for the exp model, especially for DES alone (+1.54 nats). In this case, the inferred H 0 = 70.00 − 0.98 + 4.78 ​ km ​ s − 1 ​ Mpc − 1 H_{0}=70.00^{+4.78}_{-0.98}\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}} , consistent with a full solution to the Hubble tension when judged by H ⁡ ( 0 ) H(0) . However, the excess expansion rate in this model decays on a scale z 1 < 0.086 z_{1}<0.086 , so much of it lies below the Hubble-flow window of SH0ES. The H 0 H_{0} that SH0ES would measure in this model is therefore only H 0 win = 70.23 ± 0.99 ​ km ​ s − 1 ​ Mpc − 1 H_{0}^{\rm win}=70.23\pm 0.99\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}} , which is 2.25 ​ σ 2.25\sigma below the published value (Table 4 ). This model thus reduces the Hubble tension substantially, from 6.4 ​ σ 6.4\sigma for SPA, but it does not remove it. With DES + legacy allowing recalibration, the free Δ ​ M legacy \Delta M_{\mathrm{legacy}} raises H 0 H_{0} to 69.75 − 0.98 + 1.30 ​ km ​ s − 1 ​ Mpc − 1 69.75^{+1.30}_{-0.98}\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}} , which is still short of a full solution, since SH0ES would measure only H 0 win = 69.61 ± 0.76 ​ km ​ s − 1 ​ Mpc − 1 H_{0}^{\rm win}=69.61\pm 0.76\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}} in this model, 3.10 ​ σ 3.10\sigma below the published value. The DES-only case gives a low inferred z 1 < 0.086 z_{1}<0.086 at the 1 ​ σ 1\sigma confidence level (C.L.), which suggests that the solution is localised at quite low redshift ( Nájera et al., 2026 , as also found by) . We discuss this further in Section 4.5.1 . Only when we add the SH0ES anchor on H 0 H_{0} do we get a strong preference for the exp model, with ln ⁡ B 10 = + 10.61 \ln B_{10}=+10.61 for DES and +7.87 for DES + legacy with free Δ ​ M legacy \Delta M_{\mathrm{legacy}} . In these cases, the model comes close to reproducing the SH0ES measurement itself, with H 0 win = 71.93 ± 0.67 ​ km ​ s − 1 ​ Mpc − 1 H_{0}^{\rm win}=71.93\pm 0.67\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}} for DES and 71.05 ± 0.75 ​ km ​ s − 1 ​ Mpc − 1 71.05\pm 0.75\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}} for DES + legacy with free Δ ​ M legacy \Delta M_{\mathrm{legacy}} , i.e. 1.14 ​ σ 1.14\sigma and 1.86 ​ σ 1.86\sigma below SH0ES. Their H ⁡ ( 0 ) H(0) is higher ( 75.49 ± 1.57 75.49\pm 1.57 and 72.30 ± 1.58 ​ km ​ s − 1 ​ Mpc − 1 72.30\pm 1.58\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}} ) because the excess expansion rate peaks at z = 0 z=0 and has largely decayed across the SH0ES window. We stress that the anchor is now part of the fit, so these values are not predictions. But even with the strong SH0ES anchor, the DES + legacy case (without Δ ​ M legacy \Delta M_{\mathrm{legacy}} ) still disfavours the exp model relative to Λ \Lambda CDM by 1.78 nats and predicts a low H 0 = 68.84 ± 0.70 ​ km ​ s − 1 ​ Mpc − 1 H_{0}=68.84\pm 0.70\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}} . The CPL model is at most weakly favoured by the Bayesian evidence if we add the non-SH0ES local anchors on H 0 H_{0} , with the best case being for DES + legacy without recalibration (0.87 nat preference for CPL). Adding the SH0ES anchor leads to a clear preference for the CPL model, which is 4.06 nats for DES alone. This is far weaker than the 10.61 nat preference for the exp model over Λ \Lambda CDM with the same dataset combination. Moreover, the inferred H 0 H_{0} in the CPL + SH0ES case barely exceeds 70 ​ km ​ s − 1 ​ Mpc − 1 70\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}} and has a small uncertainty, which still leads to considerable tension with SH0ES if we discard the legacy SNIa or try to rectify potential problems with them by allowing an arbitrary recalibration. The low H 0 H_{0} problem is worsened if we add the legacy SNIa at face value, since then the inferred H 0 = 68.87 ± 0.48 ​ km ​ s − 1 ​ Mpc − 1 H_{0}=68.87\pm 0.48\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}} , far below H 0 SH0ES H_{0}^{\mathrm{SH0ES}} . We attribute this to any deviation from Λ \Lambda CDM in the CPL model declining too gradually with redshift – the linear dependence of w w upon a a prevents a rapid convergence to − 1 -1 . The CPL model also has a theoretical problem in that matching the local H 0 H_{0} anchors requires w < − 1 w<-1 today and/or in the recent past. This implies a phantom fluid, violating the weak energy condition ( Sen and Scherrer, 2008 ; Lewis and Chamberlain, 2025 ) .

sections.heading: 4.5.1 Log-uniform prior on the exp model z 1 z_{1}
sections.text: Our analysis implicitly assumes that the solution to the Hubble tension lies at the background level. In this case, since it is not known a priori when deviations from Λ \Lambda CDM would start to set in, a uniform prior on the exp model z 1 z_{1} is appropriate. But if the Hubble tension is actually caused by a local underdensity or void ( Haslbauer et al., 2020 ; Banik et al., 2026c ; Banik et al., 2026a ) , then z 1 z_{1} provides an indirect measure of the void size, since the gravitational impact of a void would persist even after the density has returned to the cosmic mean ( Banik and Kalaitzidis, 2025 ) . Even so, a smaller void can generally be expected to show up in our exp model analysis as a lower z 1 z_{1} . Because we do not know a priori how large a void we might be in, a scale-free prior is arguably a better choice. We therefore revisit the above exp model results using a uniform prior on ln ⁡ z 1 \ln z_{1} , while keeping the limits unchanged. We note that a model with z 1 < 0.001 z_{1}<0.001 cannot realistically be expected to solve the Hubble tension because this would imply essentially no change to the Λ \Lambda CDM distance–redshift relation in the SH0ES range ( Riess et al., 2022 , z = 0.023 z=0.023 –0.15;) . The upper limit is less important because we will see that the results imply a low z 1 z_{1} .
